If you’ve ever felt like Call of Duty’s weapon customization requires a degree in spreadsheet management just to build a decent loadout, Modern Warfare 4 has a new solution for you. Enter Gunny, a brand-new tool designed to remove the friction of the traditional Gunsmith. Whether you’re a newcomer or a seasoned veteran, Gunny allows you to simply pick a gun and a preferred playstyle—like long-range, balanced, or close-quarters—and instantly equips a tailored, usable weapon setup based on the attachments you've unlocked.

In this video, we break down exactly how the Gunny system works in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. We explore how you can reroll playstyles to get completely different attachment combinations, swap out individual parts like a drum mag while keeping the overall build intact, and why it won't replace traditional full Gunsmith customization for those who still want total manual control. Gunny proves to be a surprisingly effective addition to the loadout process that gets

author: IGN
description:
Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy reviewed by Travis Northup on PlayStation 5, also available on PC and Xbox Series X/S.

Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy is a prequel spinoff that takes a lot of interesting chances with the series, following a new protagonist, refocusing its encounters around melee combat, and even introducing a whole new way to haunt your dreams. Some of these experiments pay off, like the new foe you eventually find yourself against and the overarching story about the ancient civilization you’ll explore the ruins of, but many more of them fall flat. That includes a significantly less compelling journey for its main character, battles that get repetitive way too fast, and light-manipulation puzzles that provide a dim flicker of amusement more often than a roaring flame. There’s still quite a bit to enjoy about Sophia’s origin story, especially if you’re just happy to be spending more time in this depressing but oddly hopeful setting – but it never came close to knockin
title: Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy Review

description:
Star Wars Zero Company reviewed by Dan Stapleton on PC, also available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

Star Wars Zero Company is an excellent tactical game that does a fantastic job of slathering on the same cinematic look and feel we saw in Respawn's Star Wars Jedi games, incorporating strong characters and a storyline that's refreshingly centered on non-Force users and a non-traditional villain. There's more of an emphasis on cooperation and flexibility, and a tighter focus on smaller maps that encourage a radically different and more aggressive playstyle. It might not have the legendary level of replayability that's kept XCOM 2 in my rotation for a decade, but its lengthy story campaign is more than worth at least a couple of playthroughs before you can see everything and get the hang of its nuanced combat and synergies.

title: 9 Minutes of Mega Man: Dual Override Gameplay

author: IGN
description:
We played Mega Man: Dual Override, which is shaping up to be a perfect entry point into the series. With Dual Override being the first mainline Mega Man game in almost a decade, Capcom have had plenty of time to think about what to do with the series. The precision platforming, tight fights, and vibrant animated stages are all there, but is this approachable take the right one?

author: IGN
description:
In the pantheon of the Persona series, its fourth entry is held in high regard, and time will tell if Persona 4 Revival will prove to be the best of the bunch. The little bit I got to see is at least making it a pretty strong contender for that award, and it still very much feels like Persona 4. But anyone who has played it before knows it’s a very long game, so we will have to wait and see whether it's worth tuning in for or changing the channel. Previewed by Scott White

#IGN #Gaming #gamescom
title: Persona 4 Revival: The Good and the Bad of Our First Hands-On-Preview – Gamescom 2026

author: IGN
description:
Get ready to restore all the Springs and revive the world. Get a closer look at Wilderings: The Lost Spring in this new trailer for the upcoming creature-collecting roguelite from Herobeat Studios. The new trailer showcases the Volcano biome along with a new boss fight, new environments to explore, more Springs to restore, and an expanded roster of Volcanic Hantu to recruit and fight alongside. Call on these new friends to help you Master the Wilds and rebuild a corrupted world in Wilderings: The Lost Spring. Wilderings: The Lost Spring will be available on PC, Xbox One, Xbox Series X/S, PlayStation 4 (PS4), PlayStation 5 (PS5), and Nintendo Switch in spring 2027.

#IGN #Gaming #gamescom
title: Wilderings: The Lost Spring - Official Gameplay Trailer | gamescom 2026

author: IGN
description:
In an age where single-player first-person shooters are slowly going extinct because they only make money for their publisher once while multiplayer live-service shooters vie for our time and attention on a daily basis (and often contain lots of bullsh*t, like microtransactions and/or drawn-out gameplay loops), Metro 2039’s single-player-only craftsmanship and attention to detail after my first few hours with it have me already prepared to call it my favorite first-person shooter in a long time.

#IGN #Gaming #gamescom
title: Metro 2039: The First Preview

description:
Step into the mysterious world of Ylem's Cat in this trailer for the upcoming action-adventure game driven by the bond between a girl and her cat. Led by curiosity and knowledge, Molly sets out on a journey to find her missing mother across a dying planet, exploring ruins and uncovering the truth buried within the giants. The trailer showcases fast-paced combat and more. Ylem's Cat will be available on PC via Steam.
